concerns.text: Task T013b (spatial_smoothing.py) is marked [P] and placed in Phase 2b, but the plan explicitly states spatial smoothing is 'deferred' and replaced by temporal smoothing for the MVP. Implementing this task violates the data-flow dependency on the approved plan scope, creating a consumer-before-producer scenario where the task consumes a non-existent plan requirement.

Task T008 is marked [P] (parallel-safe) but explicitly depends on T005 (memory_monitor.py) to enforce RAM limits before fetching. Marking it [P] implies it can run independently of T005, violating the producer-before-consumer rule for the memory constraint artifact.

Task T016b (convergence_logger.py) depends on T016 (glm_fitter.py) to generate the JSON log it parses. However, T016 is marked [P] while T016b is also marked [P]. If T016b runs in parallel with T016, it will fail to find the input artifact. The [P] tag is incorrect for T016b.

Task T029 (multi_paradigm_runner.py) is marked [P] but depends on T022 (power_curve_generator.py). The orchestrator cannot run in parallel with the core logic it orchestrates. This violates the producer-before-consumer dependency for the power curve generation artifact.

Task T007 (replication_result.py) is marked [P] but depends on T006 (simulation_config.py) as stated in its description. While models are often independent, the explicit dependency note combined with the [P] tag creates a semantic conflict if T007 is executed before T006 in a parallel batch.

Task T013c (traceability_logger.py) depends on T012, T013, and T013b. Since T013b is a scope violation (see above), T013c's dependency chain is broken. Re-ordering T013c to depend only on T012 and T013 is required once T013b is removed.
